question_text: Two clubs supply lists of member IDs, club_a and club_b. An ID can occur more than once in either list. Construct compare_members(club_a, club_b) in Python. Return a tuple containing three sets in this order: IDs in both clubs; IDs in club_a but not club_b; IDs in at least one club. Each ID must occur only once in a returned set. Set order is irrelevant. Do not modify the input lists. You may use Python set operations.
adaptation_rationale: Original coordinator-authored question for a zero-linked C2 objective; no historical source question or official marking status claimed.
solution:
def compare_members(club_a, club_b):
    a = set(club_a)
    b = set(club_b)
    both = a & b
    only_a = a - b
    either = a | b
    return both, only_a, either

Represents club_b membership uniquely as a set or equivalent set-based construction.

Returns the three sets in the requested order without modifying either input list.
